subject: API version phasing & exemption coordination
messages:
From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-22T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: API version phasing & exemption coordination

Team —

High level: the product team is proposing a phased phasing of the v1 text-generation API to push users to the v2 endpoint with improved latency and cost. There will be a mandatory default cut-off for new requests on 2027-02-01, but we need to finalize the exemption policy and the comms timeline for early customers (notably Acme).

Things I need from each of you by EOD Friday (12/24):
- Marissa: a prioritized list of customers who should be eligible for rolling exemptions and the business rationale (max 20).
- Karthik: a canary rollout schedule and fallback/runbook for cases where v2 performance regresses for production traffic. Include capacity delta and expected token-cost changes.
- Hannah: two versions of customer comms: (1) short email notice for enterprise accounts, (2) in-product banner copy. Also HubSpot sequence suggestions and required upstream CS handoffs.
- Laura: legal/terms implications — will any contract amendments be necessary for forced changes to endpoints? Flag anything that requires exec sign-off.

I attached an initial phasing matrix (phasing_matrix_v1_v2.xlsx) with my suggested 3-stage window: opt-in period (30 days), limited default (60 days), enforced cut-over. I expect exceptions to be rare but we need a tight, auditable process.

Note: Acme has asked for a 120-day exemption window in their renewal conversation (see deal notes). We should decide today whether that request is a policy exception or handled as a paid professional services add-on.

Thanks — Diego

Diego Fernandez
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-22T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API version phasing & exemption coordination

Diego —

Quick responses inline: I reviewed the product list and created a proposed exemptions_log.csv (attached). High-level:
- Recommended auto-exemptions: customers with active SSO + enterprise contracts that expire after 2027-04-01 (this gives 90+ days).
- Manual exemptions to consider: high-throughput partners where migration requires SDK/infra changes (e.g., Acme, Bytewave).
- Business rationale: retention risk + integration cost.

Questions / asks:
1) Can we offer a sponsored migration track (paid) where we provide dedicated engineering time for a guaranteed 60-day rollback/fix window? If yes, I can upsell Acme.
2) For the exemptions log: what metadata do we need to store per exemption? I suggest: customer, start_date, end_date, approver, reason, ticket_link.

I also flagged a few edge cases in the sheet (customers with long-tail on-prem deployments).

—Marissa

Date: 2026-12-22T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API version phasing & exemption coordination

Diego / all —

Read and agree with the outline. Operational items to call out:
- Canary: suggest starting with 0.5% traffic to v2 for 3 days, then 5% for 7 days, then 25% for 14 days before default changes. We can do regional rollouts (us -> eu -> apac).
- Telemetry: we will publish a shared dashboard for latency P50/P95, error_rate, token_cost_delta. Karthik will own alerts.
- Rollback: automatic fallback to v1 on per-request error-rate spike (>1.2x baseline) for 30-minute windows; manual rollback requires on-call + SRE approval.
- Capacity: v2 requires ~12% more GPU memory for the new kv-cache layout on production instance types; we have a 3-week procurement lead for spot-to-on-demand conversion.

Implication for exemptions: customers on exemptions must be tagged in routing so their traffic never routes to v2. That requires a routing key addition in the proxy layer — I estimate 2 engineer-weeks to implement and 1 week of testing.

I'll attach the draft runbook to the shared Drive (INF-4521).

—Karthik

Date: 2026-12-22T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API version phasing & exemption coordination

Diego —

Thanks — I put together two drafts and uploaded customer_notice_draft.md to the Drive link. Highlights:
- Enterprise email (short): one subject line, 3 bullets (what changes, why, what action required), CTA to request exemption or opt-in migration support.
- In-product banner: concise, link to timeline + opt-out form for approved exemptions.
- HubSpot: sequence of 3 emails over 45 days for customers flagged as "at risk"; CS to open a ticket after the second email if no response.

A few process notes:
- Exemptions must be timeboxed and recorded in our CRM (HubSpot) with an approver field (recommended: VP Sales for >60 days).
- For Acme specifically: propose a 60-day managed migration + paid services clause rather than 120-day free exemption. This is defensible and aligns incentives.

I can prepare the HubSpot sequences and push templates by Friday if we sign off on the wording.

—Hannah

Date: 2026-12-22T15:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API version phasing & exemption coordination

Diego —

Legal review quick take:
- Changing or deprecating an API we expose is within our standard TOS update language for hosted customers; however, enterprise contracts that specify an API version or provide explicit compatibility guarantees will need an amendment.
- For Acme: if they have a negotiated SLA that references the v1 endpoint by name, we should treat their 120-day ask as a contract amendment. That will require sign-off from Sales + Legal + (exec) — estimate 5-7 business days to execute.
- Data residency / compliance: exemptions that route traffic to v1 must still satisfy our audit logging and retention policies. Confirm with SRE that logs are kept for exempted routes.

Actionable: if we offer a paid migration service for 60 days, we can include a limited amendment (statement of work) rather than a full contract redline. That should move faster.

—Laura

Date: 2026-12-23T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: API version phasing & exemption coordination

Folks — quick summary and decision so we can communicate to Acme this afternoon:
- Policy: default cut-over date 2027-02-01 with the 3-stage rollout (opt-in 30d, limited default 60d, enforced cut-over).
- Acme: offer a 60-day managed migration (paid services) with a Statement of Work; decline the 120-day free exemption. Sales (Marissa) to present pricing and Laura to draft SOW language.
- Ops: Karthik to publish the canary schedule and implement routing keys for exemptions; target code + test by 2027-01-10.
- Comms: Hannah to finalize the HubSpot sequence and customer email; Diego to approve the enterprise notice.
- Audit trail: every exemption must be added to exemptions_log.csv with approver + CRM ticket id. No retroactive exemptions after the enforced cut-over.

Claire — we'll follow up with the SOW and a proposed migration schedule within 24 hours. If you want to loop legal, I've cc'd your platform alias.

Next steps (owners):
- Marissa: pricing proposal for Acme (due 12/23 EOD).
- Laura: draft SOW + short amendment template (due 12/24 EOD).
- Karthik: routing key PR + runbook (draft in INF-4521 by 01/10).
- Hannah: HubSpot sequences + email templates (12/24 EOD).

If no objections, I'll send the enterprise notice and the Acme heads-up this afternoon.

Thanks — Diego

Diego Fernandez
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
